title: Best Online Donation Software for Nonprofits in 2027
summary: Compare the 8 best online donation software platforms for nonprofits in 2027. Explore features, automation, donor management, pros, cons, and top picks.
body_markdown:
Choosing online donation software used to mean finding a reliable way to process gifts and manage donor information. Heading into 2027, nonprofits need more from their technology.The best online donation software doesn’t just help organizations collect donations. It helps them understand their supporters, automate time-consuming tasks, personalize outreach, and identify opportunities to build stronger relationships.That’s particularly important because supporters rarely engage with a nonprofit in just one way. Someone who makes a donation might also volunteer, attend an event, participate in a program, or represent a corporate partner.When those interactions live in separate systems, nonprofit teams can miss valuable connections and spend unnecessary time managing data.The right platform should make fundraising easier while giving your organization the visibility and tools to engage supporters more effectively.


Below, we compare eight online donation software platforms for nonprofits in 2027, including their strengths, limitations, and the types of organizations they’re best suited to support.

### **How We Evaluated These Platforms**


We considered several factors that matter when nonprofits evaluate online donation software:


- **Fundraising capabilities:** Online donations, recurring giving, campaign management, and payment processing.
- **Donor and supporter management:** How effectively each platform organizes constituent information and engagement history.
- **Automation:** The ability to streamline donor communications, stewardship, and administrative processes.
- **Reporting and insights:** Tools that help nonprofits understand fundraising performance and identify opportunities.
- **Ease of use and scalability:** How well each solution supports organizations as their needs become more complex.
- **Overall functionality:** Whether organizations can manage multiple activities within one platform or need additional software.


The platforms serve different organizational needs, so the best choice depends on your nonprofit’s size, fundraising strategy, existing technology, and operational priorities.


## **1. Giveffect: Best for Connected Supporter Management and Automation**


Giveffect is an[all-in-one nonprofit CRM](https://www.giveffect.com/) that brings fundraising, volunteer management, events, memberships, communications, and reporting into one connected platform.


Unlike donation tools focused primarily on processing gifts, Giveffect helps nonprofits understand the complete relationship behind every supporter.


A donor may also volunteer, attend events, participate in programs, or represent a corporate partner. Giveffect connects those interactions in a single supporter record, giving teams a more complete understanding of how people engage with their mission.


The platform also includes built-in workflow automation, helping nonprofits turn that information into timely communications, follow-up activities, and more efficient processes.


### **Pros**


**A complete view of every supporter**


Giveffect connects online and offline donations, volunteer activity, event attendance, memberships, and engagement history in one supporter record.


Rather than piecing together information across different systems, development and operations teams can see how individuals, households, and organizations engage with their nonprofit.


This helps teams identify relationships and opportunities that might otherwise go unnoticed.


**Built-in workflow automation that reduces manual work**


Giveffect’s workflow automation helps nonprofits streamline repetitive tasks and create more consistent supporter experiences.


Organizations can use[nonprofit workflows](https://www.giveffect.com/smart-automation) to support activities such as:


- Sending donor acknowledgments and personalized follow-up communications.
- Creating internal tasks and reminders for stewardship activities.
- Automating communications around supporter milestones, such as birthdays.
- Supporting donor engagement processes based on supporter activity.


For example, a nonprofit can create a workflow that sends a personalized birthday message to a donor and generates a task for a team member to follow up.


Because Giveffect connects supporter information across fundraising, volunteering, and events, teams can build processes informed by a broader understanding of each relationship.


The result is less time spent coordinating routine activities and more time available for meaningful supporter engagement.


**Smarter segmentation and personalized engagement**


Giveffect allows nonprofits to organize and segment supporters using information from across their organization.


Instead of relying exclusively on donation amounts or giving frequency, teams can identify supporters based on their broader involvement.


For example, organizations can identify volunteers who also donate, event attendees with an existing giving history, or longtime supporters who participate in multiple programs.


These insights help nonprofits create more relevant communications, strengthen stewardship, and uncover opportunities for deeper engagement.


**Reporting that helps uncover fundraising opportunities**


Giveffect provides more than 35 pre-built reports, including LYBUNT (Last Year But Unfortunately Not This Year) and SYBUNT (Some Year But Unfortunately Not This Year) reporting.


Its Mission Control Dashboard provides visibility into fundraising, volunteer activity, and supporter engagement.


Rather than simply reporting on transactions, these tools help teams recognize trends, monitor relationships, and identify supporters who may benefit from additional outreach.


### **Cons**


- As a comprehensive nonprofit CRM, Giveffect requires more implementation planning than a standalone donation form or basic fundraising tool.
- Organizations primarily looking for inexpensive donation processing may not need the full range of functionality.


### **Best For**


Growing nonprofits that manage fundraising, volunteering, events, memberships, and other supporter activities, and want to connect those functions in one system.


Giveffect is particularly well suited for organizations looking to reduce disconnected tools, automate administrative processes, and build stronger relationships using a complete view of their supporters.

## **2. Givebutter: Best for Affordability**


Givebutter is a fundraising platform designed to make online giving, events, auctions, and peer-to-peer campaigns accessible to nonprofits of different sizes.


Its fee-optional pricing model makes it particularly attractive to smaller organizations looking to launch fundraising campaigns without a substantial upfront software investment.


### **Pros**


- Fee-optional pricing lowers the barrier to entry for smaller nonprofits.
- Modern, mobile-friendly donation pages create an accessible giving experience.
- Supports online donations, recurring giving, auctions, events, and peer-to-peer fundraising.
- Built-in donor management tools help organizations track contributions and supporter activity.


### **Cons**


- Organizations with complex fundraising and operational requirements may need more extensive CRM functionality.
- Nonprofits managing multiple departments or sophisticated constituent relationships should evaluate whether the platform meets their broader needs.


### **Best For**


Small and growing nonprofits that prioritize affordability, accessible fundraising tools, and straightforward campaign management.


## **3. Bloomerang: Best for Ease of Use**


Bloomerang is a nonprofit fundraising and donor management platform known for its emphasis on donor retention and accessible CRM functionality.


It helps development teams manage donor relationships, monitor giving patterns, and identify supporters who may be at risk of lapsing.


### **Pros**


- Donor retention tools help organizations recognize engagement trends and potential lapses.
- An approachable interface can make adoption easier for teams without dedicated database administrators.
- Strong reputation for onboarding resources and customer support.
- Supports core fundraising, donor management, and reporting needs.


### **Cons**


- Advanced reporting and complex gift management requirements may require additional evaluation.
- Some organizations may need integrations or additional tools to support broader operational processes.


### **Best For**


Small to midsize nonprofits that want an approachable donor management system with a strong emphasis on retention and relationship management.


## **4. DonorPerfect: Best for Customer Support**


DonorPerfect is an established nonprofit CRM offering fundraising management, reporting, and donor tracking capabilities.


It is particularly well known for its customer support and training resources, making it an option for organizations that value ongoing assistance.


### **Pros**


- Configurable fields, reporting tools, and workflows support different fundraising processes.
- Customer support and training resources help teams adopt and maintain the platform.
- Supports gift processing, donor management, reporting, and event-related activities.
- Established functionality for managing donor records and fundraising operations.


### **Cons**


- Some users may find the interface less contemporary than newer platforms.
- Organizations with complex cross-departmental requirements should evaluate the breadth of functionality and scalability.


### **Best For**


Small to midsize nonprofits that value configurable fundraising tools, established CRM functionality, and accessible customer support.


## **5. Virtuous: Best for Donor-Centric Automation**


Virtuous is a nonprofit CRM built around responsive fundraising, an approach focused on personalized donor engagement informed by supporter behavior.


The platform emphasizes marketing automation and donor journeys that help development teams maintain relationships at scale.


### **Pros**


- Marketing automation supports personalized donor journeys and ongoing stewardship.
- Donor segmentation helps organizations tailor communications to giving behavior and engagement.
- Fundraising and CRM tools support relationship-focused development strategies.
- Automated engagement processes can reduce the time required for routine donor communications.


### **Cons**


- Organizations seeking to manage broader nonprofit operations, such as volunteer management, may need additional software or integrations.
- Pricing and functionality should be evaluated against organizational size and requirements.


### **Best For**


Midsize nonprofits focused on donor engagement, personalized communications, and automated fundraising journeys.


## **6. Blackbaud Raiser’s Edge NXT: Best for Large, Complex Organizations**


Blackbaud Raiser’s Edge NXT is a fundraising CRM designed for established development programs managing complex donor portfolios, major gifts, and institutional fundraising operations.


Its depth of functionality makes it a common consideration for larger nonprofits, foundations, and higher education institutions.


### **Pros**


- Advanced functionality supports major gift portfolios, prospect management, and complex fundraising structures.
- Moves management and portfolio tracking help frontline fundraisers coordinate donor cultivation.
- Reporting tools support sophisticated fundraising analysis.
- Connections with Blackbaud’s broader product ecosystem can support additional organizational requirements.


### **Cons**


- Implementation and migration may require substantial planning and resources.
- The platform’s depth can create a steeper learning curve for new users.
- Organizations should carefully evaluate pricing relative to database size and required functionality.


### **Best For**


Large nonprofits and established development departments managing complex fundraising programs, major donor portfolios, and advanced reporting requirements.


## **7. Neon One: Best for Small Nonprofits Seeking an All-in-One Solution**


Neon One offers nonprofit software covering fundraising, donor management, events, and memberships.


Its connected product suite is designed to help smaller organizations manage core fundraising and constituent activities without assembling numerous separate tools.


### **Pros**


- Supports donor management, fundraising, events, and memberships.
- Connected constituent information provides visibility into donor history and engagement.
- Training resources, including videos and webinars, support user adoption.
- Offers a broad range of capabilities for smaller nonprofits.


### **Cons**


- Customization may be limited for organizations with highly specific requirements.
- Teams should evaluate how easily information can be accessed and managed across the suite.


### **Best For**


Small nonprofits looking for a broad set of fundraising and constituent management tools within a connected software environment.


## **8. GoFundMe Pro (Formerly Classy): Best for Peer-to-Peer and Event Fundraising**


GoFundMe Pro is a digital fundraising platform focused on online campaigns, peer-to-peer fundraising, and event-based giving.


Formerly known as Classy, the platform helps nonprofits create branded fundraising experiences and mobilize supporters around campaigns.


### **Pros**


- Strong peer-to-peer fundraising tools support individual and team fundraising campaigns.
- Mobile-friendly donation experiences help make giving accessible.
- Recurring donation functionality supports ongoing fundraising.
- Campaign and event tools help organizations engage supporters through community fundraising initiatives.


### **Cons**


- Not designed to replace every function of a comprehensive nonprofit CRM.
- Organizations seeking extensive donor management and operational functionality may need additional software.


### **Best For**


Nonprofits that prioritize digital fundraising campaigns, peer-to-peer giving, and event-driven fundraising, particularly those already using a separate CRM.


## **How to Choose the Right Online Donation Software for Your Nonprofit**


The best online donation software depends on what your organization needs to accomplish, not simply how many features a platform offers.


A nonprofit launching its first online campaign may need a straightforward donation form, recurring giving, and basic donor tracking.


A growing nonprofit managing fundraising, volunteers, events, memberships, and multiple programs may need a more comprehensive platform that connects those activities.


Before selecting software, consider these five questions.


### **1. Do You Need Donation Processing or a Complete Nonprofit CRM?**


Donation processing software helps organizations collect and manage contributions.


A nonprofit CRM goes further by tracking relationships, engagement history, communications, and fundraising activity.


An all-in-one nonprofit CRM can also connect fundraising with volunteering, events, memberships, and other operational functions.


If your team frequently switches between systems to understand a supporter relationship, a more connected solution may provide greater long-term value.


### **2. Can the Software Automate Repetitive Tasks?**


Automation can help nonprofits maintain consistent supporter communications without increasing administrative workloads.


Look for capabilities such as automated acknowledgments, follow-up tasks, stewardship reminders, and supporter communications triggered by relevant activity.


Also consider what information the automation can use.


For example, a platform that connects fundraising and volunteer data may help teams create engagement processes informed by both types of activity, rather than donation history alone.


### **3. Does the Platform Help You Understand the Full Supporter Relationship?**


Supporters often engage with nonprofits through multiple channels.


Consider whether your software can connect donation history with event participation, volunteer involvement, memberships, and organizational relationships.


A more complete view can help teams recognize opportunities for personalized outreach and deeper engagement.


### **4. Will the Reporting Help Your Team Take Action?**


Fundraising reports should do more than summarize donations.


Look for tools that help identify lapsed donors, monitor engagement, evaluate campaign performance, and recognize opportunities for follow-up.


The most useful reporting capabilities make it easier for teams to determine what to do next.


### **5. Can the Platform Support Your Organization as It Grows?**


Consider your nonprofit’s needs over the next several years.


Will the platform support additional programs, growing constituent records, more sophisticated fundraising strategies, and increased automation?


Also evaluate implementation, training, support, and the total cost of maintaining your technology.


A lower-cost tool may be appropriate for a smaller organization, while a more comprehensive platform may reduce the need for multiple disconnected systems as operations become more complex.


## **Which Online Donation Software Is Best for Your Nonprofit?**


There is no single platform that is right for every nonprofit.


Givebutter may appeal to organizations prioritizing affordable online fundraising, while Bloomerang and DonorPerfect offer established donor management capabilities. Virtuous emphasizes personalized donor engagement and automation, while Raiser’s Edge NXT supports complex fundraising programs.


For nonprofits looking to manage more than donations, Giveffect offers a different approach.


By connecting fundraising, volunteering, events, memberships, and supporter information within one platform, Giveffect helps organizations understand the full relationship behind each gift.


Its built-in workflow automation also helps teams turn those insights into action, supporting timely communications, consistent stewardship, and more efficient operations.


For growing nonprofits managing multiple programs and supporter touchpoints, that combination of **connected data, automation, and actionable reporting** can help teams spend less time coordinating systems and more time building relationships.

An all-in-one nonprofit CRM extends that functionality by connecting additional activities such as volunteering, events, memberships, and reporting within one platform.

### Can Nonprofit Donation Software Automate Donor Follow-Up and Stewardship?


Yes. Many nonprofit fundraising platforms offer automation capabilities that help organizations maintain donor relationships.


Depending on the platform, nonprofits may be able to automate donation acknowledgments, stewardship reminders, personalized communications, and internal follow-up tasks.


Giveffect’s workflow automation can support these processes using information maintained within its connected nonprofit CRM.

### Why Does Having One Supporter Record Matter?


Supporters often engage with nonprofits in multiple ways.


Someone who volunteers regularly may also make donations, attend events, or participate in a membership program.


When those activities are stored in separate systems, teams may not recognize the full relationship.


A connected supporter record helps nonprofits understand engagement across activities, coordinate outreach, and identify opportunities for stronger relationships.


### What Should Nonprofits Prioritize When Choosing Donation Software for 2027?


Nonprofits should evaluate donation processing, recurring giving, donor management, automation, reporting, usability, and scalability.


Organizations managing multiple programs should also consider whether the platform connects supporter information across fundraising, volunteering, events, and other activities.


The right solution should support both current fundraising needs and the organization’s ability to manage relationships and operations as it grows.
